sdc.daemon.DecisionArtifact.title: DecisionArtifact
sdc.daemon.DecisionArtifact.description: What a decision request read from its case carries beside its question and its options: the recommendation, its grounds and whether the request takes a free answer (docs/engine.md, 'A request read from the case'). The runtime reads it from the case and never writes it; a request the runtime built itself has none, and only a request that has one refuses an answer that names none of its options (AnswerDecision, unknown-option).

recommended_option.description: The letter of the option the case recommends.

recommended_answer.description: A free answer the case recommends in place of an option, for a question.

recommendation_strength.description: How strongly the grounds support the recommendation; none where the request carries no recommendation.

grounds.description: The grounds of the recommendation, each with a citation the runtime checked before the request opened.

free_answer.description: Whether an answer that names no option is taken as a free answer (a question request).

sdc.decision.ArtifactId.title: ArtifactId
sdc.decision.ArtifactId.description: A case artifact id (canon-case/1 artifacts key), such as roadmap.

case.description: The case whose snapshot holds the artifact; absent means the request's case.

entry.description: One entry of the artifact, for artifact goals: the entry id (product/p1). The ground rests on that entry: it must exist in the current goals layers, apply at the check's instant (inside its validity window, not overridden by a lower layer) and still have the digest. A revision that moved since is noted (revision_moved), not refused (docs/requester.md decision 3).

digest.description: sha256:<hex> of the cited entry as sdc-goals digest prints it; written by the grounding check when absent, so a later check sees a change.

sdc.decision.CaseId.title: CaseId
sdc.decision.CaseId.description: A Canon case id (canon-case/1 id), such as IDEA-1.direction.

sdc.decision.Citation.title: Citation
sdc.decision.Citation.description: Where a ground is: path:line, a record id, artifact@revision, or one entry of an artifact (goals@<revision>#<entry id>). A program checks that each resolves (tools/decision-grounds.sh; a goals entry through sdc-goals ground).

sdc.decision.Ground.title: Ground
sdc.decision.Ground.description: One ground of a recommendation: its source kind, a citation that resolves, the option it supports (or the free answer) and how.

supports.description: The option the ground supports; absent: it supports the recommended free answer.

how.description: How the cited text supports the option, one sentence.

sdc.decision.GroundSource.title: GroundSource
sdc.decision.GroundSource.description: The kind of source a ground cites. idea: the person's own input and its dissection items (work/idea.yaml, work/dissection.yaml), which the decider cites (d1 to d4 in runs/trial-todo-1/decisions.jsonl). goals: one entry of the requester's goals document (sdc.goals/1, docs/requester.md § 2), cited as artifact_revision of artifact goals with its entry id and the entry's digest, displayed goals@<revision>#<entry id>.

sdc.decision.OptionLetter.title: OptionLetter
sdc.decision.OptionLetter.description: The letter of an option: A, B, C, in the order presented.

path.description: A file path relative to the repository root.

digest.description: sha256:<hex> of the cited lines when the ground was checked; a different digest later means the ground changed.

sdc.decision.RecordStore.title: RecordStore
sdc.decision.RecordStore.description: Where a cited record id is looked up: the decision request log, a case's evidence/ (canon-evidence/1 id), authority.json, decisions.json, or an AEP planning store (kind:name).

sdc.decision.Revision.title: Revision
sdc.decision.Revision.description: An artifact or case revision as the case snapshot writes it.

sdc.decision.Strength.title: Strength
sdc.decision.Strength.description: How strongly the grounds support the recommended option. none: the request carries no recommendation (stored before Recommend and after a withheld one; a Recommend sending none is refused). strong: a vision, requirement, PRD, story or spec states it, or a prior decision on the same question and subject stands with its grounds unchanged. moderate: a policy, an autonomy rule or an evidence record supports it by inference. weak: the grounds make it plausible only.
